Fivetran's syncing has been very reliable (compared to others we tried) but the "active row" based pricing is unpredictable and can have huge spikes in billing costs.
we've found some of their (Fivetran) competitors (who bill by connector) make far more sense for certain services. Love fivetran, though.

The fundamental challenge of open-source ETL is that high-quality connectors require understanding and working around all kinds of corner cases in the API of each data source. It's very hard to get open source contributors to do this kind of work; it's a real slog. Hence at Fivetran we've always stuck with the commercial route.
Unrelated to the article itself but Fivetran has the worst possible product from a developer perspective, their APIs are unreliable and will fail on you randomly.
Fivetran is so massively overpriced for the service they provide.

Be careful with fivetran - they inflate your data and then bill you for it. In our case, they inflated by ~10x the record count by doing a join between two tables/endpoints which wasn't required for data integrity... We dumped them once our first credit purchase ran empty.

Fivetran created a great mid-market product that was best in class and had wide adoption. What they didn't have was a very customizable product designed for large enterprises where their one size fits all strategy doesn't work.
not a big fan of fivetran's pricing

Fivetran's free plan has met my needs to sync data from different ad platforms to BigQuery pretty well. One of their pitfalls is charging by the row. If you're cost-conscious, you really need to watch what data you're syncing and pare it down quite a bit during the 2-week period they give you when setting up a new connector.

I've used Fivetran at VC funded startups... I understand the value of not having to build this piece of common infrastructure... we did experience regular (probably once every couple of months) issues with our ETL getting out of sync. We even had to do a full re-sync on a couple of occasions (which to their credit they did for no charge).

fivetran is fantastic for not having to deal with a boatload of third parties constant API updates and changes. If your core competency is something else entirely and not doing ETL, then it's worth paying for so you're not wasting time on doing that ETL work.
dbt Cloud is an uncompelling product. Fivetran is convenient but absurdly expensive.
Fivetran and dbt who are detested for being overpriced and underfeatured in the segment they are supposed to be good at (ETL/ELT).
